title: Deterministic Consensus in High-Throughput Edge Networks
summary: An empirical evaluation of zero-knowledge proof pipelines and state transition verification for distributed sensor nodes operating under intermittent connectivity.
content:
### Abstract

Modern decentralized telemetry systems deployed across rural agricultural fields or dense industrial yards encounter extreme packet drop rates, asymmetric latency, and intermittent network partitions. Traditional raft or Paxos consensus models incur excessive coordination overhead and state synchronization lockups under these physical constraints.

### The Problem: Asymmetric Latency & Packet Loss

When distributed sensor nodes collect real-time crop canopy readings, soil moisture invariants, and microclimate telemetry, standard TCP-based gossip synchronization introduces latency spikes up to 4,200ms. In high-frequency irrigation actuators, such variance causes actuation desynchronization.

### Deterministic Micro-Batches

By leveraging monotonic state machines coupled with deterministic micro-batching, nodes achieve local eventual consistency without requiring full synchronous rounds. Each local telemetry gateway generates succinct cryptographic proofs (SNARK proofs) of state transitions, aggregating hundreds of data points into a single 128-byte proof payload.

### Benchmarks & Field Results

In field trials conducted across 14 agricultural deployment zones, our edge consensus pipeline demonstrated:

- **Bandwidth Reduction**: 84.6% decrease in cellular telemetry payload size.
- **Partition Recovery**: Automatic self-healing and zero data loss during simulated 48-hour network blackouts.
- **Verification Throughput**: 12,400 proof verifications per second per core on standard ARM gateway nodes.
